name: Abdominal etching (high-definition lipo)
summary: Superficial liposuction that carves in the lines of the abs; documented in surgeon series and one systematic review, no randomized trials.
lead: Abdominal etching is a liposuction technique that removes fat at variable depths and in superficial layers to emphasize the lines of the abdominal muscles, giving the appearance of a defined abdomen or 'six-pack'. It was first described in the early 1990s and was later extended into high-definition liposculpture using VASER ultrasound technology.

name: Lymph-sparing liposuction
summary: Liposuction technique intended to protect lymph vessels, used mainly for lipedema rather than aesthetics; evidence reported as positive but limited.
lead: Lymph-sparing liposuction is a form of liposuction designed for lipedema, a chronic condition of symmetrical fat accumulation, mainly in the legs of women. Its technique is intended to protect lymphatic vessels during fat removal.

name: CoolSculpting Elite
summary: Allergan's fat-freezing system; modest, documented fat reduction with a rare paradoxical fat-growth complication.
lead: CoolSculpting Elite is a version of the CoolSculpting cryolipolysis system, a non-invasive procedure that reduces localized subcutaneous fat by controlled cooling. It is made by Allergan Aesthetics, which acquired the CoolSculpting brand from Zeltiq in 2017.

name: CoolTone
summary: A magnetic muscle-stimulation add-on to fat freezing, with almost no published evidence of its own.
lead: CoolTone is a magnetic muscle-stimulation device marketed for body contouring, and it is discussed in appearance circles as an add-on to fat-reduction treatments such as cryolipolysis ("fat freezing"), the technology behind CoolSculpting. Magnetic muscle stimulation uses a changing magnetic field to make targeted muscles contract, with the aim of increasing tone.

name: Emsculpt Neo
summary: A BTL machine that pairs electromagnetic muscle contractions with RF fat heating; reviews exist, but the studies largely use the same device.
lead: Emsculpt Neo is a non-invasive body-contouring device made by BTL Industries that combines high-intensity focused electromagnetic (HIFEM) energy, which causes strong muscle contractions, with radiofrequency (RF) heating of fat. It is marketed for increasing muscle tone and reducing fat in areas such as the abdomen, buttocks, thighs and arms.

name: Emface
summary: A needle-free RF plus facial-muscle-stimulation treatment whose headline numbers come from the manufacturer.
lead: Emface is a facial treatment from BTL Aesthetics that applies radiofrequency (RF) energy to the skin together with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation (HIFES) of facial muscles, marketed for wrinkle reduction, muscle tone and a lifting effect without needles. It is typically described as a four-session course of about 20 minutes each.

name: truSculpt iD
summary: A Cutera radiofrequency fat-reduction device with many small registered trials but few published results.
lead: truSculpt iD is a non-invasive radiofrequency (RF) body-contouring device from Cutera for localized fat reduction, with related truSculpt devices registered in trials since 2009. Radiofrequency is one of several energy modalities used for non-invasive fat reduction, alongside cryotherapy, ultrasound and laser.

name: Cavitation (ultrasonic fat)
summary: Low-frequency ultrasound devices marketed to burst fat cells; popular for DIY face-slimming, with only small registered trials and no cosmetic results found.
lead: Ultrasonic cavitation, also sold as "lipocavitation", is a non-invasive body-contouring treatment in which a handheld device applies low-frequency ultrasound to the skin over a fat deposit. Marketing and forum guides say the sound waves form tiny bubbles in the tissue that burst and break open fat cells, after which the body clears the contents.
claims: Home ultrasonic cavitation can spot reduce facial fat
Cavitation combined with radiofrequency improves targeting of subcutaneous fat
Cavitation is ineffective ("cope") and injectable fat dissolvers are better

name: Endermologie / LPG
summary: A French roll-and-suction massage machine for cellulite and contour; small studies exist, large controlled evidence is thin.
lead: Endermologie, produced by the French company LPG, is a machine-assisted massage system that rolls the skin between motorised rollers while applying suction, intended to improve the look of cellulite and body contour. It was originally developed in the late 1970s in France to soften scars and standardise physical therapy, and clinicians then noticed changes in contour and skin texture in treated patients.

name: Qwo (collagenase)
summary: A clinician-injected collagenase approved for buttock cellulite in women; bruising is a main concern and bruising is the main studied concern.
lead: Qwo (collagenase clostridium histolyticum-aaes, or CCH-aaes) is an injectable enzyme treatment for cellulite, made by Endo Aesthetics, approved as a subcutaneous injection for moderate to severe cellulite on the buttocks of adult women. The enzymes are intended to disrupt the fibrous septae that give rise to cellulite dimples.

name: Ultrasound skin tightening
summary: Heat from focused ultrasound aimed beneath the skin to tighten the face and neck; published cohort studies exist but detailed effect sizes were not verified.
lead: Ultrasound skin tightening uses intense focused ultrasound (IFUS), also called microfocused ultrasound, to deliver heat at specific depths beneath the skin while sparing the surface, with the aim of tightening and lifting sagging tissue without surgery. Branded systems such as Ulthera are used in registered trials on the face, neck and arms.

name: Microneedling (SkinPen)
summary: Branded electric microneedling pen with several small registered trials on scars, wrinkles and acne; published results were not located here.
lead: Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy, skin needling or dermarolling, is a cosmetic procedure in which tiny sterile needles repeatedly puncture the skin; SkinPen is a branded electric microneedling device used in registered clinical trials. It has been used for scarring and acne, and is combined in some practices with platelet-rich plasma.

name: Dermastamp
summary: A handheld needle-stamp used for DIY microneedling of skin and brows; no cosmetic trials found for the stamp itself.
lead: A dermastamp is a handheld microneedling tool that presses a pad of short needles into the skin in a stamping motion, as opposed to the rolling action of a dermaroller. It is discussed on looksmax.org for use on skin, brows, under-eye lines and as a way to help topicals penetrate.
claims: A dermastamp can reduce laugh lines and eye lines
Stamping the brows alongside minoxidil can support brow growth
A stamp can replace clinic microinfusion treatments

name: Jet peel (needle-free)
summary: Needle-free pressurised-jet facial for hydration and product delivery, with almost nothing published behind it.
lead: A jet peel is an aesthetic skin procedure in which a handheld device propels a fine, pressurised stream of fluid or gas (commonly saline, oxygen or a serum) at the skin surface without needles. Clinics market it for hydration, a smoother appearance and as a way to deliver topical products.

name: Hydrafacial Keravive
summary: Salon scalp facial from HydraFacial pitched for scalp health and hair quality; only registered studies, no published results.
lead: Hydrafacial Keravive (also marketed as HydraScalp) is a scalp treatment from the HydraFacial brand that adapts the company's multi-step facial platform for the scalp, aimed at cleansing, exfoliation and the delivery of topical serums to improve scalp health and hair appearance.

name: Oxygen facial
summary: Pressurised-oxygen facial that infuses serums for an instant glow; no trials of the cosmetic treatment exist.
lead: An oxygen facial is a cosmetic skincare treatment in which a handheld wand directs a stream of pressurised, purified oxygen onto the skin together with serums, typically containing hyaluronic acid, vitamins and antioxidants. It is offered for immediate hydration, a plumper look and a "glow", with no downtime.

name: LED light facial
summary: Coloured-light facial for acne and skin ageing, with small trials and preliminary evidence.
lead: An LED light facial is a clinic or at-home treatment that exposes the face to light-emitting diodes at selected wavelengths (blue, red, near-infrared and others), usually for acne, skin ageing and general skin quality. It belongs to the family of low-level light therapy, or photobiomodulation.

name: Dermalinfusion
summary: Branded exfoliate-and-infuse facial with one small published study on hyperpigmentation.
lead: Dermalinfusion is a branded aesthetic procedure that combines a form of exfoliation with simultaneous serum infusion through a handheld tip. Evidence found is limited to one 2014 Journal of Drugs in Dermatology study that combined topical delivery with dermalinfusion of decapeptide-12 to treat post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation in skin of color.

name: Jessner peel
summary: A superficial resorcinol-salicylic-lactic acid peel, also used to prime skin before TCA; evidence specific to it is thin.
lead: The Jessner peel is a superficial chemical peel based on Jessner's solution, a mixture of resorcinol, salicylic acid and lactic acid. Chemical peels are procedures in which an acid or other agent is applied to the skin to cause controlled injury, after which the skin sheds and renews itself; the general category is described as being used for fine lines, acne scarring and uneven pigmentation. Retinoic acid peels are described as commonly being preceded by a Jessner peel.

name: TCA peel
summary: A medium-depth acid peel with decades of small clinical studies for scars, pigment and photoaging, and a real burn and scarring risk when done wrongly.
lead: A TCA peel is a chemical peel using trichloroacetic acid, generally classed as medium depth and performed in a clinic or surgical setting by a medical provider. The acid coagulates skin proteins, causing controlled necrosis of the epidermis and upper dermis, followed by shedding and collagen remodelling.

name: VI Peel
summary: A branded TCA-phenol-salicylic medium peel marketed for all skin tones; published data are a few small studies.
lead: The VI Peel is a branded medium-depth chemical peel made by the Vitality Institute. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference, it blends trichloroacetic acid, phenol, salicylic acid, tretinoin and vitamin C, and is marketed for acne, pigmentation, sun damage, acne scarring, melasma and fine lines for all Fitzpatrick skin types.

name: Obagi Blue Peel
summary: A branded, standardized TCA medium-depth peel with a thin published record.
lead: The Obagi Blue Peel is a branded TCA-based medium-depth chemical peel. A 1999 Dermatologic Surgery paper described a standardized TCA-based blue peel intended to be deeper than superficial exfoliating peels while offering depth control, addressing the observation that TCA peel results vary with technique and patient selection.

name: PCA Peel
summary: A branded professional peel line from PCA Skin; manufacturer claims are not backed by independent published trials.
lead: PCA Peel is a line of professional chemical peels sold by the skincare company PCA Skin. According to a summary of the company's own materials, the brand was founded in 1990 and in 2017 Colgate-Palmolive announced it would acquire PCA Skin, a deal completed in January 2018.

name: Cosmelan peel
summary: A mesoestetic depigmenting mask-and-cream protocol for melasma and spots; claims come from the manufacturer and no published trials were found.
lead: Cosmelan is a professional depigmenting treatment developed by the Spanish company mesoestetic, marketed for melasma, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, solar lentigines and freckles. According to Grokipedia, an AI-generated reference drawing on company material, it has two phases: an in-clinic mask left on for several hours, followed by roughly six months of home cream and sun protection.

name: Dermamelan
summary: A professional non-hydroquinone depigmenting treatment for melasma, backed by one small pilot study.
lead: Dermamelan is the name of a depigmenting (skin-lightening) treatment marketed for melasma and other pigmentation, described in the literature as a non-hydroquinone bleaching formulation . It is a professional aesthetic treatment rather than a chemical peel in the classical sense, and it is discussed in appearance communities as a way to even out skin tone.

name: Retinol peel (Retinoic acid peel)
summary: A clinic-applied tretinoin peel with a few small trials in photoaging and acanthosis nigricans but no consensus protocol.
lead: A retinoic acid (tretinoin) peel is a superficial chemical peel in which a retinoid solution, often at 5% concentration in studies, is applied to the skin in a clinic and later washed off or left to act . A review describes it as a superficial peeling frequently performed in dermatological clinics in Brazil, with a first study on melasma published in 2001 . Wikipedia describes retinoic acid peels as deeper than alpha-hydroxy acid peels, used for scars, wrinkles and pigment, and often preceded by a Jessner's peel .

name: Salicylic acid peel
summary: The oil-soluble BHA peel most often studied for acne, supported by small comparative studies.
lead: A salicylic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel using salicylic acid, a beta-hydroxy acid (BHA), commonly at 20 to 30% in clinical studies and used mainly for acne and pigmentation . Wikipedia describes salicylic acid as antibacterial and anti-inflammatory and increasingly preferred over AHAs because it is oil-soluble, though the oil-solubility claim is flagged there as needing a citation .

name: Glycolic acid peel
summary: The most widely studied AHA peel, tested in melasma, periorbital darkening and acne scars in mostly small studies.
lead: A glycolic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel using glycolic acid, an alpha-hydroxy acid. Alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) are described by Wikipedia as the mildest peels, used for fine wrinkles, dryness, uneven pigment and acne . One article calls it one of the most versatile agents in melasma treatment .

name: Lactic acid peel
summary: A mild AHA peel studied in a few small comparisons for periorbital darkening and melasma.
lead: A lactic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel using lactic acid, an alpha-hydroxy acid. Alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) are described by Wikipedia as the mildest peels, used for fine wrinkles, dryness, uneven pigment and acne . Studies have used it at 15% for periorbital melanosis  and at 92% for epidermal melasma .

name: Mandelic acid peel
summary: A gentle AHA peel with only two small studies behind it.
lead: A mandelic acid peel uses mandelic acid, an alpha-hydroxy acid described as gentle in the aesthetic literature, which notes azelaic and mandelic peels are commonly used across age groups . Wikipedia's chemical peel article does not discuss mandelic acid specifically .
